page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz, the instance delivers 24 virtual CPUs across 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It features a total memory capacity of 192.0 GB, yielding a high resource ratio of 8.0 GB RAM per virtual core. The processor includes 35 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 foundation, AES, FMA, BMI2, and ADX. Network capabilities include a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth, while local disk storage and GPU accelerators are omitted in this instance type.

In performance evaluations, the server demonstrates balanced multi-core throughput alongside modest single-thread execution speeds. Single-core benchmarks reflect lower-tier performance, evidenced by a stress-ng single-core result of 1108.98 and a Geekbench single-core score of 935.0. Multi-threaded operations reach average performance tiers, marked by a PassMark CPU score of 18392.83 and a multi-core stress-ng rating of 17660.86. Memory access speeds remain standard across block sizes, measuring 984.37 GB/sec for small cached reads and 96.89 GB/sec for large uncached block reads.

From an engineering and density standpoint, the hardware profile prioritizes memory capacity over raw per-core clock performance. The lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage solutions, bounded by the 4 Gbps baseline network pipe. Database benchmarks record 16.8 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database score of 6457.08. These hardware characteristics make this instance well suited for in-memory databases, relational database engines, caching layers, and enterprise software requiring a large memory footprint without heavy single-threaded processing demands.

Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor at 2.5 GHz with 12 physical cores and hyper-threading, it provides 24 vCPUs and 192.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Operating on x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it supports AVX-512 and AES instructions with 35 MB of L3 cache. Benchmarks show average multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth performance alongside weaker single-core processing capabilities. The instance includes a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero local storage, and no GPU hardware. With a Redis SET throughput of 16.8 million operations per second, it offers a cost-effective memory footprint for enterprise applications, in-memory caching layers, relational database management systems, and memory-bound data analysis tasks.
